// ARCHITECTURE OVERVIEW
// ============================================================================

The generated files implement a complete hexagonal architecture with clear separation of concerns:

Application Layer (Input)
├─ Use Cases (Input Ports)
│  └─ Define what the application CAN DO
└─ Application Services
   └─ Implement use cases with business logic

Domain Layer
├─ Models
│  └─ Pure business entities
├─ Exceptions
│  └─ Domain-specific errors
└─ Value Objects & Aggregates

Infrastructure Layer
├─ View Mappers (Input)
│  └─ Bridge DTOs ↔ Domain Models
├─ API Adapters (Output)
└─ Gateway Adapters
   └─ Implement Gateway Ports for API calls

// ============================================================================
// ARCHITECTURAL DECISION RECORDS
// ============================================================================

1. NAMING CONVENTION
   - Domain Models: PascalCase, singular noun (Nominaxcolablist)
   - Interfaces: I-prefix optional, uses Type only for derived types
   - Methods: camelCase (findById, toFilterParams)
   - Constants: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE
   - Files: Follow domain/entity naming exactly

2. ERROR HANDLING
   - All custom errors extend AppError
   - Status codes follow HTTP standards
   - Error codes use domain_ACTION_DESCRIPTOR format
   - Field information included in validation errors

3. MAPPER PATTERN
   - All mapper methods are static (no instantiation)
   - toDomain always maps DTOs to domain models
   - toFilterParams provides pagination defaults (page: 0, size: 20)
   - All fields are explicitly mapped (no spread operator)

4. VALIDATION STRATEGY
   - Application Service validates on entry
   - Use Case contracts assume valid data from Service
   - Gateway Port communicates with infrastructure directly
   - DTOs validated during deserialization by framework

5. DEPENDENCY DIRECTION
   - Application Layer → Domain Layer (dependencies point DOWN)
   - Infrastructure Layer → Application Layer (implementation)
   - No circular dependencies
   - Domain Layer has NO external dependencies

Example: Complete Application Service Implementation Pattern

export class XxxApplicationService implements XxxUseCase {
  constructor(private readonly gatewayPort: XxxGatewayPort) {}

  async findById(id: string): Promise<Xxx> {
    if (!id) throw new XxxValidationError('ID required');
    const response = await this.gatewayPort.findById(id);
    return XxxViewMapper.toDomain(response);
  }

  async findAll(filter?: XxxFilter): Promise<XxxPageResult> {
    const params = filter ? XxxViewMapper.toFilterParams(filter) : undefined;
    const response = await this.gatewayPort.findAll(params);
    return XxxViewMapper.toPageResult(response);
  }

  async create(model: CreateXxx): Promise<Xxx> {
    this.validateXxx(model);
    const request = XxxViewMapper.toCreateRequest(model);
    const response = await this.gatewayPort.create(request);
    return XxxViewMapper.toDomain(response);
  }

  async update(id: string, model: UpdateXxx): Promise<Xxx> {
    if (!id) throw new XxxValidationError('ID required');
    const request = XxxViewMapper.toUpdateRequest(model);
    const response = await this.gatewayPort.update(id, request);
    return XxxViewMapper.toDomain(response);
  }

  async remove(id: string): Promise<void> {
    if (!id) throw new XxxValidationError('ID required');
    await this.gatewayPort.remove(id);
  }

  private validateXxx(model: Partial<Xxx>): void {
    // Add domain-specific validations
    // Throw XxxValidationError on constraint violations
  }
}
